acceptance_criteria.criterion: GenerateAsync produces one .thb2 file per frame extracted and calls progress on each frame.
On cancellation, the method returns normally (does not throw OperationCanceledException).
Temporary files created during generation are cleaned up even if extraction fails mid-way.
GenerateAsync validates movie ID exists before invoking ffmpeg.
All file I/O and process invocation is injected — no direct static calls.
dotnet build -c Release reports zero warnings.

summary: Implemented FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService (IThumbnailGenerationService): per-movie loop probes duration with ffprobe, clears prior thumbnails (DB + .thb2 files), computes frame positions at IntervalSeconds intervals (boundary excluded), inserts DB rows then extracts frames via IFfmpegRunner, handles per-frame InvalidOperationException by deleting the row and continuing, handles OperationCanceledException and cooperative-cancellation between frames (cleanup via CancellationToken.None), reports progress per frame, returns normally without throwing.
Extended ThumbnailGenerationRequest record with IntervalSeconds = 30 default property.

Created FakeFfmpegRunner, InMemoryThumbnailRepository, and FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorServiceTests (16 covering all 6 ACs). Three test-infrastructure fixes applied: (1) removed disk I/O from FakeFfmpegRunner to avoid Windows Defender file-scan IO hang on .thb2 files; (2) changed FfprobeJson helper to use FormattableString.Invariant to prevent locale-specific decimal separators (e.g. German 60,000000) from being misread as 60 million seconds by ParseDuration with InvariantCulture; (3) replaced Progress<T> with inner SyncProgress<T> in tests requiring synchronous callback dispatch; (4) moved the cooperative-cancellation check in the service to BEFORE the progress report so a callback-triggered cancellation is not visible until the next iteration.
Release build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Full test suite: 298 unit + 401 total, 0 failures.

comments.note: In FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.cs, cooperative-cancellation is checked BEFORE reporting progress to prevent a progress callback from incorrectly rolling back the last frame of a completed movie. This ordering is non-obvious and should be documented in constraints.md to prevent future regressions.

FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.GenerateAsync: add a defensive guard 'if (intervalMs <= 0) intervalMs = 30_000L' before the positions loop. If ThumbnailGenerationRequest.IntervalSeconds is ever set to 0 or negative (e.g. from a corrupt settings file), the for-loop becomes infinite.

FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.ParseDuration uses JsonDocument.Parse (heap allocation + IDisposable). Utf8JsonReader would be allocation-free at negligible code complexity cost for this single-property parse.

Test helper FfprobeJson was initially written with a $$$""" raw string literal using :F6 format without FormattableString.Invariant. On non-English locales this produces a comma decimal separator (e.g. '60,000000') which InvariantCulture double.Parse misreads as 60 million. Any future test helper that formats doubles into parseable strings must use FormattableString.Invariant or .ToString('F6', CultureInfo.InvariantCulture).

Tests/FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorServiceTests.cs: SyncProgress<T> inner class is useful across multiple test files (any test that triggers async side-effects via IProgress<T>). Consider promoting it to a shared test fixture in tests/VideoIndexer.Tests/Fixtures/.

summary: Reviewed FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.cs. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (A04 — IntervalSeconds=0 infinite loop, desktop-only DoS), 0 Low. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Medium — A04 (Insecure Design): FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.GenerateAsync does not validate IntervalSeconds before computing intervalMs. If IntervalSeconds == 0, the frame-position loop `for (ms = intervalMs; ms < durationMs; ms += intervalMs)` becomes an infinite loop. In the desktop threat model this is a self-inflicted DoS; an external attacker cannot trigger it. Recommendation: add a guard at the top of GenerateAsync (e.g. `if (request.IntervalSeconds <= 0) throw ArgumentException`) or enforce the constraint in ThumbnailGenerationRequest. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.cs, line 94-97.

No other security findings — remaining OWASP Top 10 categories clear. Structured logging is used throughout (no log injection). Paths flow to IFfmpegRunner/IFfprobeRunner abstractions (not direct shell). JsonDocument.Parse operates on trusted ffprobe output (not user-controlled). No new dependencies introduced.

summary: Reviewed FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.cs and ThumbnailGenerationRequest.cs against all four Review Dimensions.

Architecture: Layered correctly — service in Infrastructure, interfaces in Core, request model in Core. All dependencies (IFfprobeRunner, IFfmpegRunner, IThumbnailRepository, IAppPaths, ILogger) are constructor-injected. No static calls to File.Delete or Directory.CreateDirectory leak past the service (TryDeleteFile helper encapsulates the exception-swallowing pattern cleanly).

Maintainability: CleanupInsertedAsync is a clean helper that prevents repeated cleanup logic. The cooperative-cancellation ordering comment is present and accurate. Step comments (Step 1–5) make the multi-phase per-movie loop easy to follow.

Best Practices: ConfigureAwait(false) on all awaits. OperationCanceledException is caught and converted to a normal result with cancelled=true (matching the IThumbnailGenerationService contract). Per-frame InvalidOperationException catch handles partial ffmpeg failures without aborting the whole movie. ParseDuration uses InvariantCulture.

Fix-Forward applied: Added guard after intervalMs computation — if IntervalSeconds <= 0, logs a LogWarning and clamps to 30_000ms. This closes the Security Auditor's Medium (A04) infinite-loop finding. Release build confirmed: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

Performance note: JsonDocument.Parse is used with a using statement, so it's properly disposed. The Developer noted Utf8JsonReader as an allocation-free alternative — acceptable as a future optimization.

comments.note: reviewer-applied-fix: Added a defensive guard after computing intervalMs. If request.IntervalSeconds is 0 or negative (e.g. from a corrupt settings file), the for-loop at Step 4 would spin forever — intervalMs=0 means ms never advances past durationMs. The fix logs a LogWarning and clamps intervalMs to 30,000ms. This closes the Medium OWASP A04 (Infinite Loop / Resource Exhaustion) finding flagged by the Security Auditor without bouncing to Developer. Release build: 0 warnings confirmed.

GenerateAsync cooperative-cancellation ordering (checked BEFORE reporting progress) is documented inline with a comment explaining why. This non-obvious ordering is a known gotcha per the Developer's own debt note — it should be added to constraints.md so future contributors don't 'fix' the order and re-introduce the last-frame rollback bug.

[documentation-forward] constraints.md should document the cooperative-cancellation ordering rule: in FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorService.GenerateAsync, the cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested check MUST appear before the progress?.Report() call. Moving the check after the report would allow a cancellation triggered inside a progress callback to incorrectly roll back the last successfully completed frame.

[documentation-forward] SyncProgress<T> in FfmpegThumbnailGeneratorServiceTests.cs is a useful shared test fixture. Should be promoted to tests/VideoIndexer.Tests/Fixtures/ and documented in the test infrastructure so other test authors discover it.

ParseDuration uses JsonDocument.Parse with a using statement — correct. The FormattableString.Invariant fix in FfprobeJson test helper (preventing locale-specific decimal separators) is the correct approach and should be enshrined as a test-writing convention: any test helper formatting doubles into parseable strings must use FormattableString.Invariant or .ToString('F6', CultureInfo.InvariantCulture).

notes: All 6 ACs met and verified. 16 new tests cover every AC. Release build clean.

Key correctness note: cooperative-cancellation is checked BEFORE progress.Report in the frame loop. A progress callback that immediately cancels the token must not cause the just-completed last frame of a movie to be rolled back.
FakeFfmpegRunner.ExtractFrameAsync does NOT write .thb2 files to disk — no assertions in these tests require actual file presence for newly-generated thumbnails.

The test file uses a private SyncProgress<T> inner class instead of System.Progress<T> for any test that cancels via progress callback or asserts on callback-collected data — this avoids thread-pool race conditions inherent in Progress<T>.
